title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.8933: the fused pass 1 with checkpoint compares every 16th round, R = 2^24, kappa = 1.0001

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.8933 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on bradcush's 4c8222cc (125.9016: R = 2^24, h = 0.00005, p0 = 0.3900503 and kappa = 1.0001 from its shipped hazard census, unchanged) through cbea87bf, the fused-arrival package on it (125.8982), whose fused pass 1 it keeps, with one change: the checkpoint is compared only in rounds t = 0 (mod 16). Those rounds run pass1f (129.03125 per walk); the others run pass1p, the same macro without the K_cp load and the filter compare (127.03125). Anchors move to rounds t = 0 (mod 4096), so a cycle of length L <= 256 is compared at its anchored class lcm(L, 16) <= 4080 rounds later, before the next anchor; the walk's classes, escapes and endpoints are unchanged and the waste bound w < 2^-14.578 stays inside the 2^-14.56 of the kappa rule (certificate.py asserts the coverage, w and both kappa bounds). The ordinary step is 127.03125 + 444.515625 + 25616/2^20 = 571.5713 instructions; compare rounds' 2 per walk, anchor rounds' 14 and the checkpoint writes are hard rows; the traversal is step + 39 with its own end test; true filter hits are charged at twice the doubling rate. The declared run executes both copies of the fused pass 1 (548 walks, 0 mismatches) and walks 600 toy starts under the old and the production rule; the 599 that end distinguished under both reach the same endpoint (proof.md 5.2 says which rule caps the 600th). Declared dependencies (proof.md section 6): cbea87bf, 4c8222cc, 0a1c5772, 673640ef, 6a6cb91c, 610c8e49, 5f1ae3ce, 4595bad7, 2bd168b5, 01488655, daf2c741, 4b4defe7, b78fb4f6, a9297fb0, 807e4bf5, 2d25756c, b5de673a, 13c3295f, f99114e0, 02feb284. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0001*S0 = 2^126.6995074, phase 1 = 2^125.892513, hard extras = 2^113.792685, random extras = 2^99.8052, allowance = 2^114.0930, W_ledger = 2^125.8932461 < 2^125.8933; Markov ratio 0.0000441121 < 0.00005; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1258933 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1258932 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail phases, compares every 16th round) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, a check that the old and the production compare rule reach the same endpoints, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped loops (with rare exits on constructed inputs entering every stub), both copies of the fused pass 1, emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
